findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics when the file does not exist, is unreadable, or the path is invalid.
findings.failure_mode: untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire process instead of returning a typed error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) injects stdout I/O into a parsing/data-loading function that should be pure or shell-bound.
findings.failure_mode: pure logic leaks side effects into the core; output becomes polluted and the function cannot be used in contexts that capture or suppress stdout
findings.fix: remove println! entirely; logging belongs in the imperative shell layer, not in a data-loading function

findings.problem: parts[0] accessed without bounds check on a Vec built from split. Lines with zero commas yield a single-element Vec.
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (no comma) causes index-out-of-bounds panic at runtime

findings.problem: parts[1] accessed without bounds check. Lines with one comma but an empty second field, or lines with no second field, panic.
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (missing second field) causes index-out-of-bounds panic at runtime

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on any non-numeric value in the value field.
findings.failure_mode: malformed numeric input (e.g., "abc") aborts the parser instead of returning a typed parse error

findings.problem: as u16 on a u32 value silently truncates values greater than 65535. No range check is performed.
findings.failure_mode: a valid u32 like 70000 silently becomes 4448, corrupting data with no error or warning
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| ParseError::ValueOverflow) to reject out-of-range values

findings.problem: load_sessions returns Vec<Record> with no Result wrapper. All failure modes (IO, parse, overflow, missing fields) must panic.
findings.failure_mode: consumers cannot distinguish between empty file, malformed rows, and IO errors; every error path is a panic
findings.fix: signature should be fn load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> with a typed error enum

findings.problem: File I/O (fs::read_to_string) is fused with CSV parsing and domain construction. The function mixes shell concerns (disk access) with core concerns (parsing, validation).
findings.failure_mode: cannot test parsing logic in isolation; cannot substitute mock data; violates pure-core boundary
findings.fix: split into parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError> (pure core) and load_sessions(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> (shell that reads file and delegates to core)

findings.problem: Record has public fields with no validation. Any code can construct Record with empty name, invalid value, or inconsistent state.
findings.failure_mode: illegal domain states (empty name, out-of-range value) can be created anywhere without detection
findings.fix: make fields private, provide a smart constructor Record::new(name: String, value: u16) -> Result<Self, RecordError> that validates invariants

findings.problem: Vec::collect() without any prior try_reserve or input-length cap. A file with millions of lines will allocate unboundedly.
findings.failure_mode: denial of service via unbounded heap allocation; OOM on large files with no graceful degradation
findings.fix: accept a max_items parameter, validate it, call values.try_reserve(max_items).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? before collecting

findings.problem: line.split(',').map(|part| part.trim().to_string()).collect() splits into all parts and allocates a full Vec<String> just to read two fields.
findings.failure_mode: unnecessary allocation and processing of every field when only the first two are needed; split_once is the canonical one-separator approach
findings.fix: use let (name, value_str) = line.split_once(',').ok_or(ParseError::Invalid(line.to_string()))?; then parse name and value_str

findings.problem: part.trim().to_string() allocates a new String for every field including the one that is immediately discarded (extra fields beyond index 1).
findings.failure_mode: wasted allocation on intermediate parsed values that are never used
findings.fix: use split_once and only parse the two fields actually needed
